items.title: Two-group logrank and weighted logrank scores
items.statement: For two groups, define the risk-set event counts, pooled risk-set expectation, conditional hypergeometric variance, weighted score, variance estimate, normal-calibrated statistic, and the distinct exact randomization ordering. State tie and null-model conventions.

references.title: Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 6: Logrank Test, PDF pp. 1-13
Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 13: Large Sample Theory for 2-Sample Tests, PDF pp. 1-12
Michal Kulich, NMST531 Censored Data Analysis: Extended Course Notes, §5.3-5.4, PDF pp. 59-62

items.title: Uniform convergence of empirical risk-set fractions
items.statement: For iid observed times in each of two groups, the empirical fractions at risk converge uniformly on a fixed finite horizon to their population risk probabilities. Verify pointwise measurability, the unit envelope, and finite L1 bracketing entropy for the threshold class.

references.title: Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 13: Large Sample Theory for 2-Sample Tests, PDF pp. 1-12
Michal Kulich, NMST531 Censored Data Analysis: Extended Course Notes, §5.4, PDF pp. 61-62

items.title: Conditional hypergeometric moments for a logrank risk set
items.statement: When, conditional on risk-set margins, the d failures are a uniform d-subset of the Y at-risk subjects, O has mean dY1/Y and variance Y1Y0 d(Y-d)/(Y^2(Y-1)); define the variance as zero for Y=0 or Y=1. Predictable weighted increments are orthogonal under the sequential conditional model.

references.title: Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 6: Logrank Test, PDF pp. 3-4
Michal Kulich, NMST531 Censored Data Analysis: Extended Course Notes, §5.3, PDF pp. 59-60

items.title: Uniform convergence of the risk-set treatment fraction
items.statement: If n_g/n tends to an interior allocation fraction and the pooled limiting risk fraction is bounded away from zero on [0,tau], then Y1,n/(Y0,n+Y1,n), set to zero on an empty risk set, converges uniformly in probability to y1/(y0+y1).

references.title: Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 13: Large Sample Theory for 2-Sample Tests, PDF pp. 1-6
Michal Kulich, NMST531 Censored Data Analysis: Extended Course Notes, §5.4, PDF pp. 61-62

items.title: The logrank ordering gives a valid Fisher randomization p-value
items.statement: Under a finite randomized assignment law, if every unit's full right-censored event-time record is fixed under every allowed assignment, the inclusive assignment-tail p-value for the predeclared absolute weighted logrank score is superuniform. Independent continuous randomization within score ties makes it uniform.

references.title: Siva Balakrishnan, CMU 36-705 Lecture 28: Fisher's Exact p-values, §28.5, PDF pp. 4-6

items.title: Weighted logrank score expansion under a common-hazard model
items.statement: Under the separate finite-horizon counting-process model contracts, common event hazard, no simultaneous event jumps, uniform risk-set convergence, and bounded predictable weights converging uniformly in probability to a deterministic limit, the weighted score has the centered subject-martingale expansion with the limiting risk-set treatment fraction.

references.title: Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 13: Large Sample Theory for 2-Sample Tests, PDF pp. 2-7
Michal Kulich, NMST531 Censored Data Analysis: Extended Course Notes, §5.3, PDF pp. 59-60

items.title: Consistency of the weighted logrank variance estimate
items.statement: Under the explicit common-hazard counting-process contract, no simultaneous event jumps, uniform risk-set convergence, continuous event times, and bounded predictable weights with a deterministic uniform limit, the conventional weighted risk-set plug-in variance sum divided by n converges in probability to the score influence variance; no exact finite-sample hypergeometric law is asserted.

references.title: Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 13: Large Sample Theory for 2-Sample Tests, PDF pp. 4-7
Michal Kulich, NMST531 Censored Data Analysis: Extended Course Notes, §5.3-5.4, PDF pp. 59-62

items.title: Terminal normal limit for weighted logrank scores
items.statement: For two independent iid right-censored subject groups with equal continuous event hazard, conditionally independent censoring, deterministic interior allocation fractions, positive pooled risk support, the separately assumed square-integrable common-hazard martingale contracts, and bounded predictable weights converging uniformly in probability to a deterministic limit, the score divided by sqrt(n) converges to N(0, sigma_w^2), with sigma_w^2 equal to the integral of w(t)^2 y0(t)y1(t)/(y0(t)+y1(t)) against lambda(t)dt. If sigma_w^2>0, any fixed finite extension of the standardized statistic on a zero-denominator event converges to N(0,1); the result is terminal only.

references.title: Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 13: Large Sample Theory for 2-Sample Tests, PDF pp. 1-12
Michal Kulich, NMST531 Censored Data Analysis: Extended Course Notes, §5.4, PDF pp. 61-62

items.title: Crossing hazards with a zero observed logrank score
items.statement: A piecewise-exponential two-group alternative has crossing hazards and survival curves. A possible independently censored sample path has crossing Kaplan-Meier curves but logrank score zero and positive estimated variance.
items.strategy: Compute both survival functions and all nonzero risk-set contributions. Verify that the event/censoring ordering has positive probability and that the score cancellation does not establish equality of the survival laws.

items.title: An exact logrank randomization p-value with unequal assignment weights
items.statement: Three fixed event records and an unequal one-treated assignment law produce three distinct absolute logrank scores and inclusive randomization p-values whose weighted distribution is superuniform.
items.strategy: Recompute the risk sets, score, tail mass, and p-value at all three assignments, then check the exact finite weighted distribution at every threshold.
